{{Short description|European club basketball competition finals}}
{{main article|EuroLeague}}
{{Euroleague Awards}}

The '''EuroLeague Championship Game''' is the championship [[basketball]] final of the [[EuroLeague]] competition. The EuroLeague is the [[European professional club basketball pyramid|highest level tier]], and most important [[professional sports|professional]] competition of [[sports club|club]] basketball in Europe. Over the years, the EuroLeague's Championship Game, has also previously been known as the '''EuroLeague Final''', the '''EuroLeague Finals''', the '''EuroLeague Grand Final''', and the '''EuroLeague Grand Finale'''.

[[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] have won the EuroLeague championship on 11 occasions, more than any other club, with its most recent victory coming in [[2023 EuroLeague Final Four#Championship game|2023]].<ref>[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1506770/eternal-llull-gives-to-real-madrid-the-euroleague-title/ Eternal Llull gives to Real Madrid its 11th EuroLeague title]</ref> [[Olympiacos B.C.| Olympiacos]] of Greece, is the current holder of the EuroLeague championship, as of [[2026 EuroLeague Final Four#Championship game|2026]].

== EuroLeague Finals Top Scorers, MVPs, and Champion coaches (1958 to present)==
From 1958 to 1987, the Top Scorer of the EuroLeague Finals was noted, regardless of whether he played on the winning or losing team. However, there was no actual [[Most valuable player|MVP]] award given.<ref name="euroleague1958">{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/11836/180/item |title=European club champions: 1958-2011 |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2007-05-02 |access-date=2012-03-06}}</ref> On the other hand, since the end of the [[1987–88 FIBA European Champions Cup|1987–88 season]], when the first modern era [[EuroLeague Final Four]] was held, an [[Most valuable player|MVP]] is named at the conclusion of each Final Four, at the end of the EuroLeague Final.
